item.title: Kim Kardashian Held At Gunpoint In Uganda, Producer Claims In Biography
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Kim Kardashian allegedly faced a gun on a Uganda trip with Kanye West, according to a producer's biography account.
item.content:encoded:
Kim Kardashian had a police officer’s gun held to her head during a 2018 trip to Uganda with Kanye West, producer Farnaz Farjam alleged in Jonathan Van Meter’s new biography, “Citizen Kim.”

According to PEOPLE’s account of the book, Farjam said West feared being drugged and police searched rooms. She said she got her crew out on a private jet.

Viking released “Citizen Kim” on October 27. Van Meter, Vibe’s founding editor, told Forbes he spent five years working on the biography after a 2019 profile of Kardashian led him to propose a book about her.

The book drew on visits to her home, time on photo shoots and interviews with people from across her life. Van Meter told The Hollywood Reporter that she could review his manuscript for factual errors. He said she did not bar him from speaking to anyone or place topics off limits.

The couple’s Uganda visit included a meeting with President Yoweri Museveni at State House in Entebbe on October 15, 2018. His office described talks about tourism and investment. They gave Museveni a pair of white sneakers. West also pledged to build a tourism school, according to the president’s office.

The Uganda trip came two years after Kardashian survived an armed robbery in Paris, an attack that changed how she handled her security and public exposure.

In March 2017, AllHipHop reported that she cried on “Keeping Up With The Kardashians” over claims that the Paris robbery had been staged. She described the coverage as “really traumatizing.”

In the 2016 robbery, men posing as police forced their way into her Paris lodging, tied her up and took roughly $6 million in jewelry. Kardashian later told a French court that she thought she would die. A Paris court convicted eight defendants and acquitted two in May 2025.

“I learned to be more private,” Kardashian later said. “It’s not worth the risk.” The Associated Press reported that she stopped sharing her location in real time and increased her security.

Van Meter did not interview West for “Citizen Kim.” He told The Hollywood Reporter he had concerns about whether it would be ethical to do so given West’s mental health.

item.title: Usher & Chris Brown Make Touring Chart History With $77.4 Million Month
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Usher and Chris Brown became the first co-headliners to lead Billboard's monthly touring chart with a $77.4 million September.
item.content:encoded:
Usher and Chris Brown made touring chart history together, becoming the first co-headliners to reach No. 1 on Billboard’s monthly Top Tours ranking.

“The R&B Tour” earned $77.4 million from 423,000 tickets across 10 September shows, according to Billboard Boxscore.

By the October 3 show in El Paso, Texas, their first 36 concerts had grossed $284.7 million and sold more than 1.5 million tickets. That already passed the $183.9 million earned by Usher’s “Past Present Future” tour.

The win gave Usher his first No. 1 on that chart. Brown previously led it for three straight months, from July through September 2025.

This time, the pair reached the top with less money than they made earlier in the summer. July brought in $98.4 million and August added $91.8 million. Both months put them at No. 3, behind BTS and The Weeknd.

For Usher, the stadium partnership carried a point beyond his own career. Before the opening show, he told The Associated Press that R&B deserved the same large stages as other genres.

“It’s not about me and my brother coming together,” he said. “We come together in support of our fans of R&B.”

He also described the pairing as a long-held goal that stretched back to his role supporting Brown early in the younger singer’s career.

In a separate April interview, AP asked Usher about the upcoming tour with Brown. That pre-tour clip appears below.

Live Nation announced the joint stadium run in April, after the artists teased it together on Instagram. The first schedule listed 33 dates across the United States and Canada. The tour opened June 26 at Denver’s Empower Field at Mile High.

The promoter also announced a partnership with Global Citizen, pledging $1 from each ticket sold to the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund. That commitment was intended to help children gain access to education around the world.

The show itself brought the two catalogs into one production. As AllHipHop previously reported, the singers traded sections across nine acts rather than each taking a separate full set. Mario, Eric Bellinger and Tank joined the production as backing vocalists who also performed their own hits.

The reported total remained incomplete: Billboard said four October shows had not yet been reported when it compiled the figures.

item.title: Catch Concert Venue Enters Lockdown After Double Shooting Leaves Two Men Wounded
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Catch's London show faces a venue lockdown as police investigate nearby gunfire that wounds two men, leaving one with lasting injuries.
item.content:encoded:
Catch’s London concert venue went into lockdown after a nearby double shooting left two men hospitalized and one with life-changing injuries.

The South London rapper performed at O2 Academy Islington on Tuesday night as police responded to gunfire near the Angel Central shopping complex. Officers received the call at 10:25 p.m. on October 27 and found two wounded men aged 33 and 27.

Police did not consider either man’s wounds life-threatening but described the older man’s injuries as life-changing, according to The Standard’s account of the investigation. The force had announced no arrests in its latest available account and was still trying to establish what happened.

The Nightly reported that the shooting prompted a lockdown at the concert venue during Catch’s concert. The police account did not identify Catch as a target or link either wounded man to her show.

Chief Superintendent Jason Stewart, who oversees local policing, urged people with information about the attack to help officers identify those involved.

“Violence has no place in our communities, and we are pursuing every available line of enquiry to identify those involved,” Stewart said.

Live Nation listed a 9 p.m. start for her October 27 show, with doors opening two hours before the performance.

The London booking came during a year that brought Catch a Best Hip-Hop Act nomination at the MOBO Awards. Her fellow nominees included Little Simz, Central Cee, Aitch and Loyle Carner at the 30th anniversary ceremony hosted by Eve and Eddie Kadi.

Catch had also worked with Dave on “Heisenberg” after a conversation on Instagram led to time together in the studio.

“From there it was just about energy and understanding. Once we worked together, it made sense straight away,” she told Notion about their creative partnership.

Back in Islington, police put tape across part of Liverpool Road and the approach to Angel Central as they examined the scene. Stewart said extra officers would patrol the area over the following days while police worked with partners to reopen the shopping complex.

item.title: Mello Buckzz Reportedly Gets Two-Year Prison Term In Amari Blaze Case
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Mello Buckzz reportedly received two years in prison after a probation violation in the battery case involving Amari Blaze.
item.content:encoded:
Mello Buckzz reportedly received a two-year prison sentence on October 22 after admitting she violated probation in the battery case involving fellow Chicago rapper Amari Blaze.

Judge Patrick K. Coughlin resentenced the rapper, whose legal name is Melanie U. Doyle, in Cook County, according to a published account of the court records. The report said she received 197 days of credit for time already served. Her sentence also included six months of mandatory supervised release after prison.

She was first sentenced to probation. The Chicago Sun-Times reported that Mello pleaded guilty on April 17, 2025, received 30 months of probation and was ordered to stay away from Amari.

The two had once shared a record, not a court case. Amari appeared with Kashh Mir and Moni da G on “Mouskatool.” Mello also gained national attention through her Latto collaboration, “Boom Pt. 2.”

Their October 2023 clash in Calumet Park led to felony charges of aggravated battery causing great bodily harm and aggravated battery in a public place. The Sun-Times reported that court filings accused Mello of punching Amari in the face and causing her to fall through a window. The reported injuries included a broken nose and a hand wound that required tendon surgery. Her attorney, Edward L. Speights, had argued that she acted in self-defense.

A separate June 15 arrest brought a gun charge. ABC7 Chicago’s report below covered that earlier traffic stop, not the October sentencing.

Police stopped her Mercedes over an allegedly illegal windshield tint. Officers said they found a gun beneath the driver’s seat, suspected marijuana in her purse and an open bottle of alcohol inside the vehicle.

ABC7 reported that prosecutors accused her of lacking a valid Firearm Owner’s Identification card. She was charged with a felony weapons offense and two misdemeanor counts of resisting or obstructing an officer, along with traffic-related citations.

The sentencing report referenced an October 26 entry in the gun case indicating a sentence would run alongside the battery sentence. It did not establish the gun case’s full outcome or identify the conduct behind the probation violation.

An exact release date was not established in that report.

item.title: Kim Kardashian Can’t Stop Worrying About Kanye West
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Kim Kardashian described constant worry about Kanye West and the rules she used to keep their children away from family news.
item.content:encoded:
Kim Kardashian said she worried about Kanye West all day. In the new book “Citizen Kim,” she described the strain of raising their four kids.

“That’s the father of my kids, I’ll never not worry about him,” she told author Jonathan Van Meter.

She said she was still close to his family and welcomed them for dinner or time with the kids. She wanted the children to stay close to their dad.

Though her therapist urged her to set firm limits, she said she and West spoke little, clashed little and shared a hug when they met.

In the book, Kardashian also laid out house rules to shield their kids, North, Saint, Chicago and Psalm. Her “lockdown” text meant movies replaced TV. Music came from a phone in the car, with no radio, even SiriusXM, since hosts might discuss news.

Viking released the book October 27 under the full title “Citizen Kim: The Woman Who Created the Future.” The 352-page book drew on hundreds of hours of talks with Kardashian, plus dozens of her friends, family members and others close to her, the publisher said.

The book traces her rise through TV, fashion and business, along with her family life. Van Meter helped create Vibe, served as its first editor-in-chief, and has also written for Vogue and New York.

These efforts to shield the kids had roots well before the book. In AllHipHop’s December 2022 coverage of her “Angie Martinez IRL” talk, Kardashian said she stayed active in their school life. Teachers were among her close friends and helped her stay in the loop on what went on at lunch and recess.

The talk brought her to tears when she spoke of her late father, Robert Kardashian, and the good times she had with him. She wanted her own kids to have that bond with their dad, without bringing them news they had yet to hear.

Kardashian knew she couldn’t keep that news from them forever, but she hoped to shield them as long as she could.

She said her kids would one day thank her for choosing not to speak ill of their dad, despite their wild, public breakup.

item.title: Snoop Dogg Previews “I Am Me” In “Doggyland” Book Expansion
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Snoop Dogg previewed more Doggyland books, including I Am Me, as the children's series added holiday reading and activities.
item.content:encoded:
Snoop Dogg previewed the next round of “Doggyland” books in a first look shared with The Hollywood Reporter, with holiday stories and a new self-love title joining the children’s line.

The coming lineup includes “I Am Me,” which follows Bow Wizzle and the puppy crew as they learn to embrace themselves. The official listing sets its release for May 18, 2027. Elijah Williams wrote the 26-page board book for children ages 3 to 5.

Williams also wrote, “Hello, Good Morning!” It is due February 2, 2027. That 16-page book draws on the show’s “Good Morning” song, putting Bow Wizzle, Yap Yap and their friends into a read-aloud built around starting the day.

The latest release, “Ultimate Sticker & Activity Book,” reached stores October 27. Written by Juni Bright, it has 64 pages of mazes, puzzles and coloring activities, plus more than 500 stickers. BuzzPop publishes the books, with Simon & Schuster handling distribution.

For younger readers, “Jingle Bells” arrived September 29. The 18-page board book takes the shape of Bow Wizzle’s lowrider sleigh as the dogs deliver gifts around town. Its listing gives an age range of 1 to 3.

Snoop told THR the books aimed to “make sure all the kids out there know that they’re worthy and amazing.”

The books build on a deal AllHipHop covered in December, when Doggyland Media and Little Bee Books announced the publishing program.

“Affirmations Song” led that rollout. The early plans also included books about counting, family meals, breathing and eating vegetables, spreading the show’s lessons across several formats.

The publishing partnership began with an editor hearing a child rap Doggyland affirmations. Jeanine Le Ny, Little Bee’s executive editor, told Publishers Weekly that she then watched the videos and contacted the producers. The original agreement covered nine books over two years.

Snoop co-created the animated series with producer Claude Brooks and singer October London. He voices Bow Wizzle, the older dog who guides the pups, while London voices Woofee.

The music helps the characters teach kindness and helps children talk about their feelings.

Families can also meet the costumed characters December 12 at 3 p.m. at Barnes & Noble Americana at Brand in Glendale, California. THR reported that Brooks will lead storytime, followed by a sing-along, photos and stamped character autographs.

item.title: Kirk Franklin Defends GloRilla Against Gospel Critics & Haters
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Kirk Franklin defended GloRilla from religious critics and said the backlash over their gospel collaborations hurt him.
item.content:encoded:
Kirk Franklin defended GloRilla after religious critics took issue with their gospel songs. He said the backlash hurt him and didn’t give enough credit to the Memphis rapper’s success.

The gospel star addressed their work together in a Big Boy’s Neighborhood interview.

The conversation covered his faith, his approach to gospel music and the scrutiny aimed at his collaboration with GloRilla.

“It’s been breaking my heart some of the ridicule that some of the religious have given her,” Franklin said. “That she’s not holy enough or church enough to be able to do a song.”

Franklin said some critics thought GloRilla wasn’t holy enough to make a gospel song. The pair worked together on “Rain Down On Me” and “This Time.”

He also made it clear she didn’t need his help to make money. GloRilla had built her own place in Hip-Hop, he said, and he took issue with people trying to control who could talk about Jesus.

The situation hit Franklin hard when GloRilla shared her own perspective on the criticism. She pointed to scripture to make her case, asking Franklin a question that left him emotionally moved. “The Bible says that the rocks are going to cry out to God. That the rocks can praise God. That the mountains can praise God. She said, if a rock can praise God, why can’t I?” Franklin recalled. “Bro, I had no All I had was heartbreak. Because that is such a painful question.”

GloRilla’s connection to church music began well before those collaborations. In a 2023 GQ interview, she described growing up in a strict Christian home where secular music was forbidden.

She was one of 10 children and spent much of her childhood being homeschooled.

She told GQ that she and her siblings found ways to hear rap through BET’s “106 & Park” and Lil Wayne and Drake CDs they stole from Walmart. They copied music onto a PlayStation. Gospel was the music they were allowed to hear at home.

Franklin had also discussed criticism from within his own community during a separate interview with Audacy’s Big Mack earlier this month. He said he signed up for the fight to reach people with his faith and his sound more than 30 years ago.

The harder part, he said, was people close to that religious world refusing to understand his approach. He said, “what has been difficult is sometimes a rejection that you get from your own community.”

The latest discussion came as Franklin prepared to release I Am What I Am on October 30.

His current chapter also includes a partnership with Uptown Records, alongside Fo Yo Soul Entertainment and TRIBL Music Group.

AllHipHop reported the deal in September. The label founded by Andre Harrell helped build the careers of Heavy D & The Boyz, Jodeci, Guy and Mary J. Blige.

item.title: Bravo Greenlights “Next Gen Atlanta” Reality Series
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Bravo greenlit "Next Gen Atlanta," expanding its reality franchise around young people in the city's entertainment scene.
item.content:encoded:
Bravo greenlit “Next Gen Atlanta,” putting a new group of ambitious young adults at the center of the city’s Hip-Hop, sports and entertainment worlds.

The network announced the series October 23 ahead of Bravo Fan Fest in Charleston, South Carolina. The show will follow people with well-known family connections alongside others trying to build their own reputations. Their work, friendships and family lives will drive the series, which Blink49 Studios is producing.

Bravo has not named the cast or set a premiere date.

The Atlanta Journal-Constitution had already reported that the project was in production before the network made its announcement. Its Georgia filming roundup listed the first season among productions that had started work between September 4 and mid-October.

The expansion also comes as the New York show has picked up viewers. In Deadline’s report, republished by Banijay Americas, the “Next Gen NYC” Season 2 opener reached 3 million viewers across platforms within seven days, according to NBCUniversal. That was an 86% increase over the first season’s debut.

The episode also set a Bravo record for next-day viewing on Peacock after seven days. Bravo renewed “Next Gen NYC” for a third season, and production had begun, Deadline reported.

Bravo’s wider announcement also included renewals for “Southern Hospitality,” which will return for Season 5, and “In The City,” which earned a second season.

The New York series has included Riley Burruss, daughter of Kandi Burruss, and Ariana Biermann, daughter of Kim Zolciak-Biermann. Both families have ties to “The Real Housewives of Atlanta.”

In August, “Next Gen NYC” cast member Gia Giudice, Teresa Giudice’s daughter, told Us Weekly that Season 2 spent more time on the group’s personal lives and work than the show’s first season.

Bravo’s relationship with Atlanta’s music stars goes back years.

As AllHipHop previously reported, the network brought SWV and Xscape together for the six-part “SWV & Xscape: Queens Of R&B” in 2023.

That show grew out of the groups’ 2021 Verzuz matchup. Xscape had also appeared on Bravo in “Xscape Still Kickin’ It,” while Kandi Burruss had a long run on “The Real Housewives of Atlanta.”

item.title: Post Malone Previews “Bad Mood”
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Post Malone previewed "Bad Mood" as the wait for Eternal Buzz continued, following his latest comments about a huge album.
item.content:encoded:
Post Malone shared another taste of The Eternal Buzz on October 28, previewing a song apparently called “Bad Mood” while the album wait continued.

According to Billboard, the Instagram clip showed him listening on a couch with a beer. His #badmood hashtag suggested the title, while his caption again teased the album as coming soon. Billboard heard echoes of his beerbongs & bentleys era in the new snippet.

The preview followed another big claim about the size of the project. During his performance at the Formula 1 United States Grand Prix, Post told the crowd the record had around 50 songs, according to Holler. That number was larger than the two sets of 20 tracks shown when he first teased the project in April.

Questions about his next sound were already part of the conversation this summer. AllHipHop covered a separate July preview that had listeners talking about his return to rap after his country pivot. That clip included a reference to Stoney, his 2016 album. The possibility of a record divided between country and rap remained a theory in that report, which tied the renewed interest to the melodic sound of Stoney and beerbongs & bentleys.

His catalog gives both groups of listeners a reason to pay attention. Twelve Carat Toothache included appearances from Roddy Ricch, Doja Cat and Gunna. On F-1 Trillion, Post worked with Morgan Wallen, Tim McGraw and Dolly Parton. The latter record also paired him with Jelly Roll on “Losers” and Luke Combs on “Guy For That.” Those albums show the range behind the genre question surrounding his next project, from rap guests to established country stars.

The Grand Prix update offered another sign of how large he was thinking, though a rough count from the stage was not a final tracklist. The earlier April image pointed toward 40 songs across two discs. His latest estimate put the total closer to 50. At the same performance, he thanked fans for their support over the years and told them the new music was on its way. He also warned the crowd to “Listen in moderation” when the record arrived.

item.title: Too $hort Explains How Cash Demand From The Pack’s Friends Led To Signing
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Too $hort recalled The Pack's friends seeking money for an introduction before he signed the group behind the 2006 hit "Vans".
item.content:encoded:
Too $hort said The Pack’s friends demanded money for an introduction without the group knowing.

In his new Pitchfork interview, he recalled hearing their mixtape and meeting the friends at a hamburger stand. After calls revealed one member was his friend’s son, he reached out and signed them.

“We sitting in front of a hamburger stand and they like, ‘We ain’t the Pack, but the Pack is our homies, but you can’t get to the Pack unless you go through us ‘… they was just talking about how much money they gonna be getting from me. That was so unprofessional. I did my due diligence and called around and found out one of the dudes in the Pack was my homeboy’s son…That was their homies; they intercepted the call to try to get something out of it. The Pack didn’t even know,” Too $hort revealed.

The deal worked out well. According to $hort, he took them on the road, and the group was popular everywhere they went. The group also introduced him to MySpace.

His interest in the group fit a wider push for young Bay Area acts. In a 2006 San Francisco Chronicle interview, he said he wanted hyphy to create jobs and major-label deals.

He helped The Pack reach Jive while leaving their music in their hands. He said he didn’t make their beats or choose their song titles. His role was to spot talent and give it a shot.

That support also showed up on his own label’s releases. The Pack joined the lineup of I Love The Bay, a compilation released July 17, 2007. It put the group on a project with E-40, Keak Da Sneak, Messy Marv, Yukmouth and San Quinn, among others.

The album also included Zion I, The Team and a posthumous appearance by Mac Dre. Its track list paired The Pack with Mistah FAB on “Yes Sir.” The first singles were “Lose It,” featuring Mistah FAB and “Video Vixen,” featuring Dem Hoodstarz.

“I always wanted to represent the entire Bay Area,” Short said in AllHipHop’s coverage of the compilation. The release gave that aim a concrete form, with younger acts and established names sharing the same album.

The Pack’s own business moved on from Short’s label.

As AllHipHop reported in 2010, the Berkeley group included Lil Uno, Stunnaman, Lil B and producer Young L. They had been signed to his Up All Nite imprint, with distribution through Jive Records.

Their 2006 single “Vans” had sold more than 300,000 copies by May 19, 2010, when SMC Recordings announced a deal with them. The plan called for an album titled Wolfpack Party, with The Cataracs among its guests.

SMC’s interest had started before that deal. Will Bronson, then the company’s chief operating officer, said he tried to sign The Pack when “Vans” broke, but competing with Too $hort got in the way.

Too $hort told Pitchfork that he is still cool with the group and that he brings them out on stage to perform “Vans” to this day.
